label: O'Connor's EMOTIVISM_1 and the existence of a moral sentence are jointly satisfiable
meaning: O'Connor's emotivism as a complete rival theory (#185): his four recorded readings (moral statements have no truth value; what has none is not true; there are no objective moral truths; badness ascriptions are moral; #157/#160) are jointly satisfiable with the existence of a moral sentence. One of the four, 'there are no objective moral truths', is recorded from his 2016 subjectivism (O'Connor-Turek), not from his 2023 emotivism (DISAMB-MORAL-ANTIREALISM): the bundle is O'Connor's recorded metaethics, not emotivism alone, and nothing here derives that reading from emotivism. His prescriptive element ('don't murder') is not yet formalized: re-reading his spans needs the youtube-corpus export (#184). Its answer map and counts are in TruthCore.Comparison.Metaethics.
